findings:
🟠 [wdog-alive-check-fail-open] MUST-FIX The new pre-fire gate in `_arm_worker_watchdog` (`if ! _watchdog_worker_alive; then exit 0`) turns any failure to *prove* liveness into a silent non-enforcement: `_watchdog_pgid_has_live` returns 1 whenever `ps -e -o pgid=,state=` yields nothing (ps fork failure under pid/memory exhaustion by the very runaway worker being bounded; non-procps `ps` lacking the `state` keyword), and the SCOPE_UNIT branch treats an empty `ps -o state= -p "$rp"` as dead. Result: watchdog exits, `wait "$rp"` never returns, run hangs unbounded while `timeout_enforced: true` is reported. Pre-diff the watchdog still fired when `ps` failed (empty selfpg only skipped the self-guard; `kill` is a builtin). Smallest fix: distinguish "ps produced no output" from "group has only zombies": in `_watchdog_pgid_has_live` do `out="$(ps -e -o pgid=,state= 2>/dev/null)" || return 0; [ -n "$out" ] || return 0` and iterate over `$out`; in `_watchdog_worker_alive` treat an empty rp state as unknown (fall through to the pgid check, and if that also has no ps output, return 0). Fail toward firing, since the group-kill on an already-dead group is harmless (ESRCH unstamps `.fired`).
🔵 [pgid-has-live-forks] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_watchdog_pgid_has_live` spawns two `$(printf|tr)` subshells per process on the host per check; `read -r pgid st` already strips IFS whitespace, so drop the `tr` lines. Excluded: runs once at deadline, correctness unaffected.
🔵 [test-reap-pid-dead-pid] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Test helper `reap_pid` issues bare `kill -KILL "$pid"` on pids read from stub pidfiles even after `wait_pid_dead` confirmed them dead (r8 tail, r2 failure paths); guard with `pid_alive "$pid" &&` or a `/proc/$pid/cmdline` check. Excluded: test-only, requires pid recycling inside a few seconds; no pkill/pgrep patterns are used, so no broad-match kill risk.
🔵 [test-set-e-leak] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Both r6 tests run `set -e -o pipefail` at file scope and never restore it; `-o pipefail` stays on for every later test. Wrap the eval+call in a subshell or `set +e +o pipefail` before returning. Excluded: later tests reset `set +e` and currently pass.
🔵 [test-assert-eq-arg-order] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Most new asserts pass the literal first (`assert_eq "false" "$(json_get …)"`) while lib.sh is (actual, expected) per the RED output, so failure text reads "expected 'true', got 'false'" inverted. Cosmetic, equality check is unaffected.
🔵 [cgroup-set-m-tty-bg-pgrp] CUT/FOLLOW-UP New `set -m` on the cgroup path places the worker in a background pgid relative to a controlling tty when the dispatcher is run from a terminal; a worker CLI that reads `/dev/tty` would now stop on SIGTTIN instead of blocking in the foreground, until the watchdog KILL (TERM stays pending on a stopped process). The added `</dev/null` correctly restores the implicit stdin redirection bash drops under job control. Excluded: workers are non-interactive prompt-file CLIs; consider `setsid systemd-run …` instead of job control as the isolation primitive.
